collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder)

collection.description: An elder moving nearer the water must hand the old garden plot to another villager: introduce every plant, or just hand it over.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is moving to a hut nearer the water, where the path is flatter and the walk to the fire is shorter. It's a good decision. (subject.He/she) made it (subject.him/her)self. But it means giving (subject.his/her) old garden plot to (friend), and this morning (subject) is walking slowly along the rows, touching each plant as (subject.he/she) goes.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) walks (friend) up and down the rows, explaining. This one likes to be talked to. This one is a liar and will look dead in the dry season, but isn't. This one was planted the year (subject) had (subject.his/her) first grey hair. (friend) listens to all of it. It takes the whole morning, and neither of them minds.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "It's yours," says (subject), and hands over the digging stick. "Look after it." (friend) promises (friend.he/she) will. (subject) walks away without looking back, which takes some effort. A few days later (friend) brings (subject.him/her) the first ripe melon from the plot. (subject) eats it slowly, and says it's very nearly as good as the ones (subject.he/she) used to grow.
